identities.label: Stentinello culture
identities.description: neolithic culture in Sicily and Calabria
identities.summary:
Stentinello culture was a middle Neolithic culture, widespread in Sicily and Calabria, dated to the fifth millennium BC. Under different names this culture is also present in the Aeolian islands (Castellaro Vecchio culture) and Malta (Għar Dalam phase). The Kronio culture, a variant of that of Stentinello, was widespread in western Sicily.
In the eponymous site were found the remains of buildings with rectangular plan enclosed in a ditch dug in the rock forming an oval space of about 180 x 200 meters. The burials of this culture, found in various places in Sicily, but not in Stentinello, were oval pit carved into the rock in which the deceased lie buried in a crouched position.
